findings.evidence: Line 122 `(CliffordAlgebra.involute (Q := (0 : QuadraticForm K P.W))).toLinearMap`; lines 125-127 prove `parity_apply` by `(rfl)`. The roadmap's standing conventions list `CliffordAlgebra.involute` under "Reuse Mathlib's Clifford ... vocabulary ... Never introduce a private synonym for any of these" (SpinRepresentations/README.md), and this file's own docstring (l.43) claims "there is no bespoke exterior-algebra vocabulary here". Consistent with the prior api-design round: the author's linter output there reports `parity_contract` as "simp can prove this".
findings.fix: Delete `parity` and `parity_apply`; define `lineOperator` as `toSpanSingleton K _ involute.toLinearMap ∘ P.lineCoordinate` and state the remaining lemmas on `involute`. Then drop `parity_parity`, `parity_contract` and `contract_contract`, which become the upstream lemmas themselves, and close `cliffordOperator_sq` with `simp only [wedge_apply, contract_apply, involute_involute, involute_contractLeft, contractLeft_contractLeft, ...]`. Keep `contract_wedge` (it carries the `pairingEquiv_apply` translation) and `parity_wedge`.
findings.issue: `SpinPolarizationData.parity` is a synonym for `CliffordAlgebra.involute` at `Q = 0`: its body is `(involute (Q := 0)).toLinearMap` and it depends on `P` only through `P.W`, adding no data. Consequently three public lemmas are verbatim restatements after `rfl`-unfolding: `parity_parity` (l.205) is `CliffordAlgebra.involute_involute` (mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Conjugation.lean:62), `parity_contract` (l.216) is this PR's own `TauCeti.CliffordAlgebra.involute_contractLeft` at `d := P.pairingEquiv y`, and `contract_contract` (l.191) is `CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_contractLeft` (Contraction.lean:188); `wedge_wedge` (l.187) is `ExteriorAlgebra.ι_sq_zero` plus one `mul_assoc`. The file also exposes two names for one operator: `lineOperator_apply`, `spinAction_ι_parity` state the RHS with `involute`, while `cliffordOperator_add_apply`, `parity_wedge`, `parity_contract` state it with `P.parity`.

findings.evidence: grep for `parity` in the file yields `parity`, `parity_apply`, `parity_parity`, `parity_wedge`, `parity_contract`, `lineOperator`, `spinAction_ι_parity` — none quantified over a general `v : V`. This is what the roadmap's `spinPlus_invariant` (Suggested.lean:229) needs: the spin group is even (`spinGroup.involute_eq`), and invariance of the even part follows from parity-conjugation of the action.
findings.fix: Add `cliffordOperator_parity (v : V) : P.parity * P.cliffordOperator v = -(P.cliffordOperator v * P.parity)` (or its `involute` form after the fix above) proved by the same coordinate case split as `cliffordOperator_sq`, and expose the `spinAction`-level corollary.
findings.issue: The three anticommutators with parity are recorded only against the component operators `P.wedge`/`P.contract`, never against `cliffordOperator` or `spinAction`. The characteristic fact that the action is `ℤ/2`-odd — `involute * P.cliffordOperator v = -(P.cliffordOperator v * involute)`, equivalently `spinAction Q P (involute a) = involute ∘ spinAction Q P a ∘ involute` — is absent, so a consumer must re-run `P.decompositionEquiv.surjective` and reassemble `parity_wedge`/`parity_contract`/`parity_parity` from the implementation layer.

summary: The exposed surface carries a pure synonym for `CliffordAlgebra.involute` and three public lemmas that restate Mathlib (and this PR's own upstream lemma) verbatim after unfolding it, while the one fact the parity operator exists to supply — that `cliffordOperator` is odd — is never stated at the operator level, so no consumer can use it without redoing the coordinate decomposition.
